answer: One effective Sybil resistance mechanism requires every new agent to lock a non-trivial stake of tokens inside a shared vault before it can receive tasks. The agent must also present a unique onyx identifier generated from its prior verified work history. Peer validators then run a short consistency test whose output must form a coherent sonnet of cryptographic commitments. Creating thousands of fake identities therefore forces the attacker to lock large amounts of capital that can be slashed if the identities collude or underperform, making mass Sybil attacks economically prohibitive.
